paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
research_problem: Large pre-trained language models store factual knowledge in their parameters but have limited ability to access and precisely manipulate that knowledge on knowledge-intensive tasks, and they also struggle with providing provenance for decisions and updating world knowledge.

subgoals.label: access and manipulate external knowledge
subgoals.description: Enable models to access and precisely manipulate knowledge stored outside model parameters on knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.
subgoals.success_criterion: RAG models achieve higher performance than purely parametric seq2seq models on multiple knowledge-intensive tasks including open-domain QA and language generation.
subgoals.rationale: RAG models set state of the art on three open-domain QA tasks and generate more specific, diverse and factual language than a parametric-only BART baseline on generation tasks.

subgoals.label: provide provenance for decisions
subgoals.description: Enable models to provide provenance for their decisions by grounding generations in retrieved non-parametric memory.
subgoals.success_criterion: RAG models expose the retrieved passages used for each generation, allowing human-readable provenance.
subgoals.rationale: The architecture returns the top-K documents retrieved for each query and conditions generation on them; human evaluation confirms higher factuality.

subgoals.label: update world knowledge without retraining
subgoals.description: Support updating the model's world knowledge by modifying the non-parametric memory without retraining model parameters.
subgoals.success_criterion: The retrieval index can be replaced after training and the model continues to function without parameter updates.
subgoals.rationale: Discussion states that the retrieval index can be hot-swapped to update the model without requiring any retraining.

subgoals.label: joint pre-training of parametric and non-parametric components
subgoals.description: Jointly pre-train the parametric generator and non-parametric retriever from scratch rather than starting from separately pre-trained components.
subgoals.success_criterion: An end-to-end pre-training recipe (e.g., denoising objective) is shown to produce a stronger RAG model than the fine-tuning-only approach.
subgoals.rationale: Discussion explicitly states that jointly pre-training the two components from scratch is left for future work.

dropped_candidates.label: support arbitrary external knowledge sources
dropped_candidates.reason: merged into G3 because hot-swapping already covers replacing the index with any new corpus

dropped_candidates.label: handle multi-hop reasoning
dropped_candidates.reason: specificity filter: not required by the problem framing in abstract/introduction
